cohort: Women giving birth at >20 weeks gestation or with a fetus weighing >400g in Australia and New Zealand
finding: The incidence of placenta accreta was high at 44.2/100,000 births, and was associated with increased risk of caesarean section, hysterectomy, maternal death, preterm birth, and neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: Women with placenta accreta were more likely to have a caesarean section.
